# aeneid-087 — drafter's notes (XI.532–647)

57 units, 116 lines; `t` cut by `A.cut` in `make_units.py`; all script checks pass with no warnings (the four
EXEMPT units below are skipped by the mark checks only). Every unit is at most five lines and ends at
punctuation. Part name "Camilla's Childhood and the Cavalry Battle (XI.532–647)"; Latin title
"Camillae infantia. Pugna equestris". Paragraphs (p): 532, 597.

## Speech marks
- Diana's speech runs 535 `“Graditur` to 594 `reponam.”` without a break. Reason: at 537–538 she names herself
  in the third person (`novus iste Dianae venit amor`), and again at 582 (`sola contenta Diana`), as gods do in
  their own speeches; 539–583 is the story she tells Opis, and 584 `Vellem` continues in the first person with no
  verb of speaking. So:
  - 537 `”Neque`: a closing mark joined to the next word, treated as a rule-5b misprint (precedent QUESTIONS
    55/56/59/64). t as printed; l/i carry no mark; the note of unit 537 opens "The print has a closing double mark
    joined to 'Neque'…".
  - 584 `“Vellem`: the matching faulty reopening mark. t as printed; l/i carry no mark; the note of unit 584 opens
    "The print has an opening double mark before 'Vellem'…".
- Metabus's prayer 557 `“Alma` – 560 `auris.”` is nested inside Diana's speech: l/i give it single marks ‘ … ’
  (precedent 084, 085). Units 557 and 559 notes open by saying so.
- Unit 535 (opening “) and unit 593 (closing ”) carry the marks in l/i exactly as in t.
- EXEMPT = {537, 557, 559, 584} (unit ln). No other unit starts on those lines.

## Misprints corrected under rule 5b (t as printed, l/i read the correction, note opens with the print)
- 588 `abere` → `labere` (Latin Library `labere`). `abere` is no Latin form (abeo's imperative is `abi`); the sense
  needs the deponent imperative `labere`, 'glide down', which Opis obeys at 595 `delapsa`. Note of unit 587 opens
  "The print has 'abere', a misprint for 'labere', corrected here."
- 625 `scopulusque` → `scopulosque` (Latin Library `scopulosque`). `superiacit` is transitive and needs an object;
  `unda` is ablative and `spumeus` agrees with `pontus`; a nominative `scopulus` leaves the verb objectless and the
  rock as an impossible second subject. Treated as a misprint; note of unit 624 opens
  "The print has 'scopulusque', a misprint for 'scopulosque', corrected here…". A reviewer who prefers caution
  could downgrade this to "doubtful, kept", but I could not construe the printed form.

## Doubtful / variant readings kept as printed
- 613–614 `ruina … dant sonitum ingenti` (Latin Library `ruinam dant sonitu ingenti`): the print construes
  ('with a huge crash they make a sound'), so kept; the variant ('they make a fall with a huge sound') is mentioned
  in the note because it shifts the sense slightly (crash vs. downfall).
- 539 `viresque` (LL `uirisque`): orthography/morphology only (-es/-is acc. pl.); both are accusatives governed by
  `ob` with `invidiam`. Construction explained in the note; variant not mentioned.
- 569 `aevom`, 591 `volnere`, 614 `quadrupedantum`, 626 `arenam`: orthography; Greenough's forms explained, LL
  variants not mentioned.
- 639 `vulneris` is printed with u although 591 has `volnere`; noted in passing in unit 638.

## Interpretive choices to check
- 630 `bis reiecti armis respectant terga tegentes`: subject taken as the Etruscans (continuing `Tusci`, the
  ebb of the simile); the note gives the alternative (the Rutulians). l keeps an ambiguous "they"; i says
  "they were thrown back in their turn".
- 612 `Tyrrhenus` taken as a proper name (an Etruscan on the Trojan side), as usually printed with a capital.
- 552–555 anacoluthon (`Telum… huic… hastae`) explained as the object put first and resumed.
- 641 `cui` + supplied verb ('he had') for the description of Herminius.
